conventions.convention: A hereditary Hall category is supplied small and F_q-linear, with finite-dimensional Hom and Yoneda Ext¹ and vanishing Yoneda Ext²; enough projectives or injectives are not assumed.
The product [M] ⋆ [N] counts sequences 0 → N → L → M → 0 and multiplies their subobject count by ν raised to dim Hom(M,N) minus dim Yoneda Ext¹(M,N), with ν = √q > 1 and coefficient field Q(ν).

P^R_{M,N} counts endpoint-labelled exact sequences; the Green coefficient is ν^{χ₀(M,N)} P^R_{M,N}/a_R. The completion contains all coefficient functions, but multiplication is extended only where every output coefficient is a finite sum.
Extended Hall elements use actual left-torus normal order k_α[M]; moving k_β left past [M] contributes ν^{−(β,[M])}.
The chosen extended coproduct sends a simple class to [S_i] ⊗ k_i⁻¹ + 1 ⊗ [S_i], matching Δ(E_i) = E_i ⊗ K_i⁻¹ + 1 ⊗ E_i; the alternative positive Hall convention is kept separate.
For a finite loopless quiver with oriented cycles, the Hall category consists of finite-dimensional nilpotent representations; acyclic quivers use all finite-dimensional representations.
The integral specialization at ν⁻¹ has the positive Green tensor twist after relabelling half generators. Its identification with the numerical Serre-only presentation is a separate theorem.
Finite Dynkin means every connected underlying multigraph component is finite ADE; disconnected and empty quivers are included.

load_bearing.statement: For fixed M,N,K,L in a finite-field hereditary Hall category, the automorphism-weighted count of pairs of exact sequences with common middle object equals the four-edge square count weighted by |Yoneda Ext¹(K₂,L₁)|/|Hom(K₂,L₁)|; both sums are finite.

Assuming inherited Choice, for a finite symmetric Cartan datum with d_i = 1 and ν = √Q for a prime power Q > 1, the normalized Kashiwara form specializes nondegenerately on every finite homogeneous component of the actual integral halves at ν and ν⁻¹, whose dimensions are the classical PBW ranks.

There is a surjective graded algebra map from the actual integral half specialized at ν⁻¹ onto the quiver Hall composition algebra, sending F_i to [S_i] and preserving the homogeneous Green-normalized form; its component dimensions are consequently at most the classical PBW ranks.

Assuming inherited Choice, for every finite symmetric generalized Cartan matrix and either parameter ν or ν⁻¹, the algebra presented by the numerical symmetric quantum Serre relations is canonically the actual Lusztig integral-half specialization.
For the numerical symmetric Serre algebra at real q > 0, q ≠ 1, a nonzero homogeneous element z killed by both i-skew derivatives satisfies Σ_j a_ij deg_j(z) ≤ 0.

If J/S is nonzero for the kernel J of the free negative half's map to the actual specialization and the numerical Serre ideal S, a least-height nonzero residual degree −β satisfies (β,β) = 2 ht β > 0.

On bounded-above Q-label-graded modules of the actual integral specialization U_t, t ∈ {ν,ν⁻¹}, the constructed natural Casimir commutes with U_t and acts on a highest vector of label λ by t^{(λ,λ)+2 ht λ}.

For a finite loopless quiver over F_q, with the stated nilpotent convention, its vertex-simple-generated composition subalgebra equals the full Hall algebra if and only if every connected underlying multigraph component is finite ADE.

The specified small skeleton of finite-dimensional nilpotent representations of a finite loopless quiver is a finite-field hereditary Hall category, with vertex simples S_i, K₀ ≅ Z^{Q₀}, and dim Yoneda Ext¹(S_i,S_j) = c_ij.
For extensions E: 0 → A → B → C → 0 and F: 0 → C → D → X → 0 in an abelian category, their splice is zero in Yoneda Ext²(X,A) exactly when F is the pushout along B → C of an extension of X by B.
For any orientation of an affine D or E tree over F_q, there are constants c > 0 and m₀ such that every m ≥ m₀ admits at least cq^m/m nonisomorphic indecomposables of dimension mδ.

concerns.concern: The Statement and Given do not declare inherited Choice, although F3 invokes thm-integral-triangular-decomposition-for-the-lusztig-form for finite freeness and classical PBW ranks. That supplier's Statement explicitly begins 'Assume the Axiom of Choice'. The proof's PBW dimension conclusion therefore uses a hypothesis not carried into this item's stated assumptions. The same issue affects presentation of this lemma as an unconditional supplier.

Step 3.1 concludes finiteness of the coefficient of '[S] ⊗ [R]', whereas the Statement, F2 and steps 1.1–2.1 fix and analyze '[R] ⊗ [S]'. The objects are arbitrary, so this does not invalidate convergence, but the final displayed order is reversed.
